web.title: Strict URI Matching - Meta for Developers - Facebook
web.description:
# Strict URI Matching
#### By Phillip Hodgson
All redirect URI's used by an app need to be listed in the **Valid OAuth redirect URIs** list in the app's Login Settings in order to be used in our OAuth flow. The first exception is that apps with an empty list of **Valid OAuth redirect URIs** were grandfathered into being allowed to receive tokens on any endpoint on their domain. The second exception is that redirect URIs are allowed to "prefix match", meaning any URI that is prefixed by a URI on the list of Valid Oauth URIs would be valid.

You can also use our **Redirect URI Validator** on the Facebook Login settings page to see if you have any links impacted by this change.

If you need to update your redirect URIs, follow our developer documentation on how to [enable Strict Mode](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/facebook-login/security#strict_mode).

Redirect URI error with the new Instagram Login
web.description:
In our Meta Developer Dashboard at [https://developers.facebook.com/apps/208543671492761/instagram-business/API-Setup/?business\_id=928042731242983](https://developers.facebook.com/apps/208543671492761/instagram-business/API-Setup/?business\_id=928042731242983), we have configured a single redirect URI under "3. When we initiate Step 1 (Get authorization) by directing users to the authorization URL with our client ID (1459320281888548), our redirect URI, and the requested scopes (instagram_business_basic and instagram_business_manage_insights), everything works correctly. The user successfully authenticates with Instagram, and Instagram redirects back to our configured redirect URI with the authorization code appended.

Please make sure your redirect_uri is identical to the one you used in the OAuth dialog request"

First, we only have one redirect URI configured in the dashboard, so there's no possibility of using different URIs.

Second, we're using the identical redirect URI in both the authorization request and the token exchange request, copy-pasted to ensure they match exactly. Third, if our redirect URI wasn't properly registered, the first step would have failed with an "invalid redirect_uri" error, but it succeeds, proving our URI is valid and recognized. We've tried both with and without trailing slashes, we've made sure the encoding is consistent, and we've verified the URI character by character.

Despite all these efforts, we keep receiving the same error claiming our redirect URIs don't match, which seems impossible given our configuration.
